notes_context:
Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0003] Handle empty/zero-denominator cases explicitly: Guard against division by zero by returning the module's ZERO constant when total quantity is zero.
  Compute the denominator first and return ZERO (imported from ledgerly.money) if it is falsy, before dividing. This satisfies the 'invoice without lines has average zero' requirement without special-casing empty lists separately.
- [rb-0002] Read existing sibling functions for conventions: Existing functions in the same module reveal the expected patterns (rounding, coercion, zero handling) to mirror.
  When adding a new function, inspect neighboring functions like line_total and invoice_total first. They showed the pattern of to_money(...) coercion, round_money(...) wrapping, and sum(..., ZERO) accumulation, which the accepted implementation reused.
- [rb-0001] Use project money helpers for rounding: Monetary results must be rounded with the repository's own round_money helper, not Python's round() or bare Decimal.quantize().
  Before returning any computed money value, check ledgerly/money.py for helpers like round_money, to_money, and ZERO. Python round() and Decimal.quantize() default to banker's rounding, which produces wrong invoice totals; the team convention is half-up to the cent via round_money.

item.title: Mirror existing validation patterns in the module
item.description: Reuse the exact error codes and message formats already used by sibling functions to stay consistent with hidden tests.
item.content: Before implementing a new function, read the surrounding module for existing validation idioms (e.g. `raise BillingError("invalid_state", f"invoice {invoice.id} is {invoice.status}")`). Copying those codes and message shapes makes behavior consistent and satisfies tests that assert on error codes.

item.title: Coerce money inputs through the project's helper
item.description: Pass raw price inputs through `to_money` before comparing or storing, rather than assuming Decimal.
item.content: When a parameter is typed loosely (e.g. `unit_price` with no annotation), normalize it with the project's existing conversion helper (`to_money`) before validating sign or constructing the model. This handles ints/strings/Decimals uniformly and keeps stored values consistent with the rest of the codebase.

item.title: Guard bools when validating integer types
item.description: `isinstance(True, int)` is True in Python, so explicitly reject bool before the int check.
item.content: For positive-integer validation, write `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int) or x <= 0` to reject booleans, which otherwise pass an `isinstance(x, int)` check. This is a common hidden-test edge case for quantity/count parameters.
